problems.reason: Both sentences state that a 2020 study by Adam Marsh and Timothy Rowe classified Cryolophosaurus as a basal neotheropod.
Both sentences state that pathologies on Cryolophosaurus bones show evidence of scavenging behavior.
Both sentences claim the crest was used for intraspecific recognition.
Sentence 21 classifies Cryolophosaurus as a derived neotheropod closely related to Averostra, while sentence 22 classifies it as a basal neotheropod.
Sentence 23 gives an age range of 186–182 Ma, whereas sentence 24 gives 196–188 Ma for the same species.

Sentence 26 says the classification remains debated due to mixed traits, while sentence 27 states new studies in 2007 demonstrated it was probably a ceratosaurian more closely related to Dilophosaurus and Dracovenator.
Sentence 28 challenges the idea that the crest was for mating, fighting, or intimidation, whereas sentence 29 disputes the species recognition function and suggests a socio‑sexual display model.

Both claim the animal is the largest known theropod from the Early Jurassic, but sentence 19 classifies it as a derived neotheropod, implying a different taxonomic status inconsistent with the claim of being the largest known theropod.
